summary: Household: New Mexico, 4 people (two married parents, two children under 18, none under 5), household earnings about $80,700/year, owns home with about $500/month housing cost. Recommended now: (1) CHIP (New Mexico children's health coverage): at about 245% of the federal poverty level for a family of four, the children likely qualify under New Mexico's higher children's limit; apply through BeWellNM or Medicaid/CHIP. (2) Child Tax Credit, refundable part: with $80,700 earned income and two qualifying children, the family should qualify; claim when filing taxes. Not recommended: SNAP, TANF, SSI, WIC, school meals, and EITC (income is above the limits for each). Adult Medicaid is not available at this income. ACA premium tax credit (aca_ptc) may apply only if no affordable job health coverage is offered; the family could not say whether they have job coverage, so a caseworker should confirm this before applying. Assets were also not confirmed, though they do not affect the recommended programmes. Hand off to a caseworker to verify employer coverage and income.
